questions.stem: A 28-year-old male presents with painless lymphadenopathy, night sweats, and weight loss. A lymph node biopsy is done following which a diagnosis of nodular sclerosis Hodgkin lymphoma is made. Which of the following statements about this condition is false? EBV NegativeMediastinum is rarely affectedCollagen bands are present in cellular areasPoor prognosis compared to classical HL
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) 2 and 4  

 

Mediastinum is commonly affected and has good prognosis. It is EBV negative and collagen bands are present.   

 

2. Mediastinum is rarely affected - False

 

  • Nodular sclerosis HL frequently involves the mediastinum, especially in young adults, particularly females.
  • It's one of the most common sites of involvement in NSHL.
  • So this statement is false.

 

4. Poor prognosis compared to classical HL - False

 

  • Nodular sclerosis is a subtype of classical HL
  • It actually has a relatively good prognosis, especially when detected early.
  • Lymphocyte-depleted HL has the worst prognosis among classical subtypes.
  • So this statement is also false

 

Correct Statements:

 

1. EBV Negative - True (mostly)

 

  • EBV association is variable:
  • Nodular sclerosis subtype is less strongly associated with EBV compared to mixed cellularity subtype.
  • So this statement is generally true.

 

3. Collagen bands are present in cellular areas - True

 

  • In nodular sclerosis, broad bands of collagen divide the lymph node into nodules — hence the name.
  • This histologic hallmark is what gives the subtype its name.
  • So this statement is true.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old male presents with fatigue, pallor, and shortness of breath on exertion. Laboratory results show hemoglobin of 8.5 g/dL, mean corpuscular volume (MCV) of 115 fL, and a peripheral blood smear revealing hypersegmented neutrophils and macro-ovalocytes. Further testing shows elevated methylmalonic acid (MMA) and homocysteine levels. Anti-intrinsic factor antibodies are negative. What is the most likely cause of his anemia?

options.label: B
options.text: Vitamin B12 deficiency due to dietary insufficiency

questions.answerText: Vitamin B12 deficiency due to dietary insufficiency
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Vitamin B12 deficiency due to dietary insufficiency

 

  • Folate deficiency: elevated MMA is specific to vitamin B12 deficiency (not folate deficiency)
  • Vitamin B12 deficiency (elevated MMA and homocysteine levels are specific indicators of vitamin B12 deficiency)
  • Myelodysplastic syndrome: less likely in the presence of elevated MMA and homo levels.  Also, MDS typically associated with abnormal bone marrow findings.
  • The absence of anti-intrinsic factor antibodies, ruling out pernicious anemia.

questions.stem: A 15-year-old tall and slender male with long limbs presents with multiple painless mucosal nodules on the lips and tongue. His father died because of some cancer in the neck. Physical examination reveals a ganglioneuroma on the posterior tongue. Genetic testing confirms a mutation in the RET proto-oncogene. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2B (MEN2B)

 

Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2B (MEN2B) is an autosomal dominant genetic disorder caused by mutations in the RET proto-oncogene. It is the most aggressive subtype of MEN2 and is characterized by specific clinical features: Mucosal neuromas, Marfanoid habitus, Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma and Pheochromocytoma (hypertension and episodic symptoms such as headaches, palpitations, and sweating.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old male with an undiagnosed malignancy presents to the emergency department with diffuse petechiae, purpura, and mucosal bleeding. Laboratory investigations reveal thrombocytopenia, prolonged prothrombin time (PT) and activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT), decreased fibrinogen levels, and schistocytes on peripheral blood smear. Which of the following factors is most likely contributing to the pathogenesis of his condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) AML t(15;17)

 

Patient presentation:

 

  • Diffuse petechiae, purpura, mucosal bleeding → signs of bleeding tendency
  • Labs show:
    • Thrombocytopenia
    • Prolonged PT & aPTT
    • Low fibrinogen
    • Schistocytes → suggest microangiopathic hemolysis

 

All these are classic features of DIC, a consumptive coagulopathy.

 

Which leukemia is strongly associated with DIC?

 

Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia (APL) → AML with t(15;17)

 

  • t(15;17) → fusion of PML-RARA gene
  • APL is notorious for triggering DIC due to:
    • Release of procoagulant granules from abnormal promyelocytes
    • Activation of clotting cascade → consumption of platelets and clotting factors
    • Risk of life-threatening hemorrhage, especially intracranial or pulmonary

 

Other Options:

 

 

  • DIC in a patient with undifferentiated leukemia → think of APL
  • APL = AML with t(15;17) = M3 subtype
  • Requires urgent therapy with all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA) to prevent fatal bleeding

questions.stem: A 68-year-old male presents to his primary care physician with complaints of increasing fatigue, unintentional weight loss, and easy bruising over the past few months. Physical examination reveals palpable lymphadenopathy in the cervical and axillary regions. Laboratory investigations show an elevated white blood cell count with a predominance of small lymphocytes. Flow cytometry analysis reveals co-expression of CD5 and CD23 with dim expression of surface immunoglobulin. Which of the following additional findings is most likely to be present in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Autoimmune hemolytic anemia

 

CLL is often associated with autoimmune complications, with autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA) being one of the most common. This process can exacerbate fatigue and contribute to the patient's symptoms. AIHA is more common than other cytopenias like thrombocytopenia (Option D). Hypochromic microcytic anemia (Option A) is not typical of CLL and may suggest an alternative diagnosis, such as iron deficiency anemia. Hypercalcemia (Option C) is not a common finding in CLL.

questions.stemHtml: A patient presented with complaint of a jaw swelling. His tissue was found to have the presence of t (8;14). The histopathological appearance of the bone marrow aspirate tissue is given in the image. Which of the following is a likely diagnosis for this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Burkitt lymphoma

 

The presence of a translocation t(8;14) is characteristic of Burkitt’s lymphoma. The same is confirmed by the tumor cells with cytoplasmic vacuolation and distinct nucleoli.

Direct lines from Robbins…”When the bone marrow is involved, aspirates reveal tumor cells with slightly clumped nuclear chromatin, two to five distinct nucleoli, and royal blue cytoplasm containing clear cytoplasmic vacuoles”.

questions.stem: A 10-year-old boy presented with complaints of recurrent bleeding. He has a retroperitoneal hematoma and develops joint pain with swelling on slight exercise. There is no mucosal bleeding in the patient. Which of the following coagulation factor can be responsible for the patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Factor 8/9 deficiency

 

The presence of recurrent deep tissue bleeding (retroperitoneal hematoma and develops joint pain with swelling on slight exercise) in a male is suggestive of a clotting factor deficiency.

 

  • Amongst the clotting factor deficiency, the deficiency of factor 8/9 is more commonly observed in comparison to factor 9/12 deficiency.  
  • Absence of mucosal bleeding helps to rule out von willebrand disease.  
  • Lupus anticoagulant shall be usually asymptomatic. It is seen with pregnancy and has an elevated aPTT.

questions.stem: A 50 year old patient has malaise for 2 weeks. His investigation s revealed an elevated creatinine of 4.5mg/dl. His blood tests also showed the presence of HBs antigen. A renal biopsy was performed which demonstrated spike and dome on special staining. Which of the following conditions is the patient likely to be suffering from?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Membranous glomerulopathy

 

The elderly patient is having a renal dysfunction. The presence of a ‘spike and dome’ pattern on special staining is suggestive of immune complex deposition. This is characteristic of membranous glomerulopathy. The diagnosis id also supported by the presence of HBs antigen as the hepatitis B infection is characteristically associated with development of membranous glomerulopathy.

questions.stem: A 56 year old chronic smoker presented with complaints of weight loss and cough for more than 1 year. He also has hypercalcemia. His biopsy report revealed hyperchromatic atypical cells. Which of the following is the most likely cancer is this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Squamous cell cancer

 

The presence of hyperchromatic atypical cells on biopsy with the given clinical history suggests a cancer. The history of chronic smoking with hypercalcemia as a paraneoplastic syndrome is a finding of squamous cell cancer of the lung.  Hence, the answer is option “b”.

questions.stem: A 4-year-old patient presented with a rectal mass 2.5 cm by 3 cm. On biopsy it had the presence of colonic mucosa with multiple dilated glands filled with mucin and inflammatory cells. Which of the following is a likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Hamartoma

 

The clinical history of a rectal mass on biopsy having the colonic mucosa with multiple dilated glands filled with mucin and inflammatory cells is suggestive of a juvenile polyp. This polyp is an example of a hamartomatous polyp. So, the answer is option b.

questions.stemHtml: A 32-year-old female presents to her primary care physician with complaints of palpitations, weight loss, and heat intolerance. On physical examination, she has a diffuse, non-tender goiter and lid lag on upward gaze. Her image is given alongside. Which of the following antibodies is most likely to be elevated in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) Thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulins

 

Graves' disease is has auto-antibodies like thyrotropin receptor antibodies (TRAb) which stimulate the TSH receptor and increase T3 and T4. Anti-thyroid peroxidase (anti-TPO) antibodies (Option A) and anti-thyroglobulin (anti-Tg) antibodies (Option B) are more commonly associated with Hashimoto's thyroiditis. Thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulins (TSI) (Option D) are a subtype of TRAb and are specifically implicated in the pathogenesis of Graves' disease.

 

  • This case describes a 32-year-old woman with:
    • Symptoms of palpitations, weight loss, and heat intolerance (suggestive of hyperthyroidism)
    • Diffuse, non-tender goiter
    • Eye signs- specifically lid lag and the image shows exophthalmos (proptosis)
    • These features are classic for Graves disease, an autoimmune cause of hyperthyroidism.
  • Most likely elevated antibody:
    • Thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulins (TSI)

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Anti-thyroid peroxidase (anti-TPO): Seen in Hashimoto thyroiditis (hypothyroidism), sometimes in Graves too but not diagnostic.

 

Option B. Anti-thyroglobulin (anti-Tg): Also common in Hashimoto and thyroid cancers, non-specific.

 

Option C. TSH receptor antibodies (TRAb): Broad category that includes both stimulating and blocking antibodies. TSI is a type of TRAb, but for Graves disease, TSI is the specific driver.

 

Conclusion:

 

Graves disease → hyperthyroidism + eye signs

questions.stem: Which of the following suggest a programmed cell death not involving caspases? Apoptosis NecrosisPyroptosisNecroptosisFerroptosis
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) 4, 5

 

  • Programmed cell death (PCD) can occur through various mechanisms, some involving caspases (a family of protease enzymes), while others do not.

 

4. Necroptosis is a form of programmed cell death that does not involve caspases. Instead, it uses receptor-interacting protein kinases (RIPK1 and RIPK3) and the mixed lineage kinase domain-like protein (MLKL), making it a caspase-independent pathway.

 

5. Ferroptosis is another form of programmed cell death. It is an iron-dependent process and is not related to caspase activity. Ferroptosis is characterized by the accumulation of lipid peroxides, leading to cell death, and does not involve any caspases.

 

Both necroptosis and ferroptosis are examples of caspase-independent programmed cell death, which is why the correct answer is C (4, 5).

 

Other Options:

 

1. Apoptosis: Apoptosis is the most well-known form of programmed cell death, which relies heavily on caspases (such as caspases 3, 6, 7, 8, 9). Therefore, it does not fit the criteria for this question.

 

2. Necrosis: Necrosis is not a programmed form of cell death. It is an uncontrolled, passive process resulting from injury, infection, or other environmental stress, and does not involve any caspase activity or signaling pathways.

 

3. Pyroptosis: Pyroptosis is a form of programmed cell death associated with inflammation. It involves caspases (particularly caspases 1, 4, 5, and 11), making it a caspase-dependent process.

 

Necroptosis and ferroptosis are programmed cell death mechanism but neither involves caspases.

questions.stemHtml: Match the following stains with their respective tissue:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) 1-a, 2-b, 3-d, 4-c

 

1. Prussian Blue (1-a: Iron): Prussian blue stain is used to detect iron deposits in tissues. It turns iron deposits blue.

 

2. PAS (Periodic Acid-Schiff) (2-b: Glycogen): PAS stain is commonly used to highlight glycogen, mucopolysaccharides, and other carbohydrate-rich structures, staining them a magenta color.

 

3. Congo Red (3-d: Amyloid): Congo red stain is specific for amyloid deposits, which appear red under light microscopy and show apple-green birefringence under polarized light.

 

4. Fite Faraco Stain (4-c: Leprosy): Fite Faraco stain is used primarily to identify Mycobacterium leprae, the bacterium causing leprosy, in tissue samples.

 

Educational Objective:

questions.stemHtml: A physician wanted to perform plasma glucose estimation using the vacutainer shown in the image. Which of the following is the anti-coagulant used for this test?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Potassium oxalate

 

The vacutainer shown in the image is used for plasma glucose estimation, and it contains potassium oxalate as the anticoagulant. Potassium oxalate works by binding to calcium, preventing blood clotting.

 

In addition to the anticoagulant, sodium fluoride is often added to these vacutainers to inhibit glycolysis, which preserves glucose levels by preventing the cells from metabolizing the glucose in the sample. The combination of potassium oxalate (anticoagulant) and sodium fluoride (glycolysis inhibitor) is typically used in glucose collection tubes.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Sodium fluoride: While sodium fluoride is present in the tube, its primary role is to inhibit glycolysis, not as an anticoagulant. The anticoagulant in this case is potassium oxalate.

 

Option C. EDTA: EDTA is used as an anticoagulant in tubes for complete blood counts (CBCs) and other hematological tests but is not used for glucose estimation.

 

Option D. Trisodium citrate: Trisodium citrate is primarily used for coagulation studies (e.g., prothrombin time and activated partial thromboplastin time) and is not used for glucose estimation.

 

Educational Objective:

 

  • For plasma glucose estimation, the tube contains potassium oxalate as the anticoagulant and sodium fluoride as a glycolysis inhibitor. Both work together to preserve the glucose level for accurate measurement.
  • Always use a grey-top tube (NaF/KOx) when measuring plasma glucose to prevent post-collection glycolysis and falsely low results.

questions.stem: A 50-year-old woman presents with a family history of breast and ovarian cancer. Genetic testing reveals a mutation in the BRCA1 gene. Which of the following best describes the function of BRCA1?

options.label: A
options.text: Encodes a cell surface receptor for growth factors

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Repairs double-strand DNA breaks

 

The BRCA1 gene is a tumor suppressor gene that plays a crucial role in the repair of double-strand DNA breaks. Mutations in BRCA1 are associated with an increased risk of breast and ovarian cancers.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old female presents with fatigue and pallor. She was diagnosed with TB few months back and has been taking her medications regularly. On examination, her peripheral blood smear shows ringed sideroblasts. Which of the following are likely to be seen in her blood investigations? Reduced serum iron levelReduced transferrin saturationReduced total iron binding capacityIncreased ferritin level
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) 3, 4

 

  • 32-year-old woman with fatigue and pallor
  • History of tuberculosis (TB) on anti-TB drugs
  • Peripheral smear shows ringed sideroblasts

 

This points toward sideroblastic anemia, likely drug-induced, most commonly due to isoniazid (INH).

 

 What is Sideroblastic Anemia?

 

  • A type of microcytic anemia where iron is available, but cannot be incorporated into hemoglobin.
  • Mitochondrial defect in heme synthesis → iron accumulates in the mitochondria of erythroblasts → forms ringed sideroblasts (seen on Prussian blue stain of bone marrow).

 

Common Causes:

 

  • Drugs: especially Isoniazid (INH) (interferes with vitamin B6, needed for ALAS enzyme in heme synthesis)
  • Alcohol, lead poisoning, copper deficiency, myelodysplastic syndromes

 

Iron Profile in Sideroblastic Anemia:

 

 

Other Options:

 

1. Reduced serum iron: False. serum iron is increased in sideroblastic anemia

 

2. Reduced transferrin saturation: False. transferrin saturation is increased

questions.stemHtml: A 7-year-old child presents with morning headache, nausea, and vomiting. On examination, there is truncal ataxia and signs of increased intracranial pressure. MRI reveals a midline mass in the cerebellum with heterogeneous enhancement. A biopsy is performed, and histological examination shows small, round, blue cells with Homer-Wright rosettes. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Medulloblastoma

 

Medulloblastoma: highly malignant, arises in the cerebellum, predominantly in children. It typically presents features of increased ICP. On imaging, it appears as a midline mass in the cerebellum.

 

Histologically, has small, round, blue cells with a high N:C ratio. Homer-Wright rosettes, and disseminates CSF pathways.

questions.stem: A child with skin rash, reduced platelet count and high risk of infections should be evaluated for:

options.label: A
options.text: B cell tyrosine kinase activity detection

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) WASP gene mutation

 

As it is likely case of Wiskott Aldrich syndrome.

 

A child with:

 

  • Skin rash (often eczema-like)
  • Thrombocytopenia (low platelet count)
  • Recurrent infections
  • This classic triad points to:
    • Wiskott-Aldrich Syndrome (WAS)

 

 Wiskott-Aldrich Syndrome Features:

 

 

  • X-linked recessive
  • Caused by mutation in the WASP gene, which is critical for cytoskeleton rearrangement in hematopoietic cells

     

Other Options:

 

Option A. B cell tyrosine kinase activity detection: Refers to Bruton’s agammaglobulinemia, which presents with recurrent bacterial infections but no thrombocytopenia or eczema

 

Option C. Adenosine deaminase activity:Refers to ADA-SCID, which causes severe T and B cell immunodeficiency, but not thrombocytopenia or eczema

 

Option D. CD40 defect on B cells: Refers to Hyper-IgM Syndrome (class switching defect), presents with infections, but no thrombocytopenia or eczema

questions.stem: A 60-year-old male presents with a history of metastatic lung adenocarcinoma. He has been receiving chemotherapy but recently developed resistance to the current treatment regimen. The oncologist recommends a liquid biopsy to assess for genetic mutations and guide further therapy. Which of the following techniques is most commonly used in liquid biopsy for the detection of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA)?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Next-generation sequencing (NGS)

 

Next-generation sequencing (NGS) is the preferred method for liquid biopsy in detecting circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA). NGS allows for the simultaneous detection of multiple genetic mutations in ctDNA, providing comprehensive genomic profiling of the tumor. This information helps guide treatment decisions, especially in cases of acquired resistance to therapy, as in this patient.

 

Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) (Option A) is a sensitive technique but is limited to the detection of specific mutations (point mutation).

Immunohistochemistry (IHC) (Option C) and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) (Option D) are primarily used in tissue biopsy specimens rather than liquid biopsies.

questions.stem: Which of the following is incorrect about invasive lobular carcinoma of the breast?

options.label: B

options.label: C

questions.answerText: There is over-activity of CDH1 gene
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) There is over-activity of CDH1 gene

 

There is UNDER-activity of CDH1 gene leading to reduced expression of E-cadherin and so, bilaterality and multifocal.

questions.stem: A patient has presented to the hospital with features of cutaneous vasculitis, synovitis, increased blood pressure and RBC casts in the urine. He has a history of hepatitis C infection few weeks ago. Which of the following is the likely lesion seen in his renal biopsy?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Membranoproliferative glomerulopathy

 

Essential mixed cryoglobulinemia is another systemic condition in which deposits of cryoglobulins composed principally of IgG-IgM complexes induce cutaneous vasculitis, synovitis, and a proliferative glomerulonephritis, typically MPGN. Most cases of essential mixed cryoglobulinemia have been associated with infection with hepatitis C virus, and this condition in particular is associated with glomerulonephritis, usually MPGN type I.

questions.stem: Identify true statements about familial adenomatous polyposis? Autosomal recessive inheritance with late presentationIf not treated, all cases progress to adenocarcinoma colon.KRAS mutations cause familial adenomatous polyposisIt is associated with congenital hypertrophy of the retinal pigment epithelium.
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A) 2 and 4

 

Statement 2. If not treated, all cases progress to adenocarcinoma colon: True

 

  • 100% risk of colorectal carcinoma by middle age (~40 years) if prophylactic colectomy is not performed
  • Hence, early diagnosis and intervention are critical

 

Statement 4. It is associated with congenital hypertrophy of the retinal pigment epithelium (CHRPE): True

 

  • CHRPE is a characteristic extraintestinal manifestation of FAP
  • Seen as pigmented lesions in the retina on ophthalmic examination

 

These are the true statements regarding familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP).

 

Incorrect Statements:

 

Statement 1. Autosomal recessive inheritance with late presentation: False

 

  • FAP is autosomal dominant, not recessive.
  • Caused by a mutation in the APC gene on chromosome 5q
  • Presents early in life (teens or early adulthood) with hundreds to thousands of colonic adenomatous polyps

 

Statement 3. KRAS mutations cause familial adenomatous polyposis: False

 

  • KRAS mutations are seen in the adenoma-carcinoma sequence, especially in sporadic colorectal cancer
  • FAP is caused by a germline APC gene mutation, not KRAS

questions.stem: A 30-year-old female presents with excessive bleeding following a minor injury. She has no personal or family history of bleeding disorders. Laboratory testing reveals a prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) that does not correct after mixing her plasma with normal plasma. What is the most likely cause of her symptoms?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) Acquired factor VIII inhibitor

 

In this patient with no personal or family history of bleeding disorders and a prolonged aPTT that does not correct after mixing studies, the most likely cause of her symptoms is an acquired factor VIII inhibitor (Option d).

questions.stem: A 40-year-old female presents with a rapidly growing abdominal mass. Biopsy of the mass reveals a high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma. Metabolic profiling of the tumor tissue shows elevated levels of lactate and decreased mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation. Immunohistochemical staining demonstrates overexpression of hexokinase II and hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha (HIF-1α). Which of the following processes is most likely driving the metabolic phenotype observed in this tumor?

options.label: A
options.text: Upregulation of the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle

options.label: C
options.text: Activation of the pentose phosphate pathway

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) Enhanced aerobic glycolysis

 

The metabolic phenotype observed in the tumor, characterized by elevated lactate levels, decreased oxidative phosphorylation, and overexpression of HK-II and HIF-1α, is consistent with the Warburg effect. Cancer cells upregulate glycolytic enzymes, such as hexokinase II, to enhance glucose uptake and metabolism, leading to the accumulation of lactate. HIF-1α activation, often induced by hypoxic conditions within the tumor microenvironment, further promotes glycolysis and inhibits mitochondrial function. The Warburg effect allows cancer cells to meet their increased energy demands and promote biosynthesis to support rapid proliferation.

 

  • TCA cycle (Option A) and fatty acid oxidation (Option B) are typically downregulated in cancer.
  • Activation of the pentose phosphate pathway (Option C) can occur in cancer cells to generate NADPH and pentose sugars for nucleotide synthesis but is not the primary driver of the metabolic phenotype observed in the Warburg effect.

questions.stem: A 56-year-old man presents with dragging pain in the abdomen. On examination, there is massive splenomegaly. Peripheral smear shows leukocytosis with increased myelocytes, metamyelocytes and basophils. Which of the following translocation is seen in this condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Correct answer: A - t(9;22)

The clinical pattern is consistent with chronic myeloid leukemia, whose Philadelphia chromosome is the reciprocal translocation t(9;22), producing the BCR::ABL1 fusion. questions.stem: A 60-year-old male presents to his physician with concerns about aging-related health issues. He has a family history of cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Further investigation reveals dyslipidemia and impaired glucose tolerance. Research studies suggest a potential role of sirtuins in promoting longevity and improving metabolic health. Which of the following actions is most likely mediated by sirtuins?

options.label: A
options.text: Stimulation of insulin secretion from pancreatic beta cells

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Inhibition of NF-κB-mediated inflammation

 

Sirtuins are a family of NAD+-dependent protein deacetylases that play critical roles in regulating various cellular processes, including metabolism, stress response, and aging.

Sirtuins cause inhibition of NF-κB-mediated inflammation (helps in cardiovascular disease and type 2 DM). Sirtuins deacetylate and inactivate NF-κB, a transcription factor involved in the regulation of inflammatory responses.

 

Option A & D: are not the direct function of sirtuins.

 

Option B: sirtuins may indirectly influence mTOR signaling, they do not directly activate it.

questions.stem: A 42-year-old woman presents with a painless breast lump. Clinical examination reveals a palpable, firm, non-tender mass which on mammogram shows an irregular mass with spiculated margins and microcalcifications. A diagnosis of breast cancer is made. Which of the following is correct about the disease? Most common location is the upper outer quadrant of her left breast. Usually arises from terminal duct lobular unit. Nulliparity is protective Molecular classification of breast cancer is based on gene expression profiling.
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) 1,2,4

 

Early age of menarche, nulliparity, absence of breastfeeding, and older age at first pregnancy are all associated with increased risk.

Gene expression profiling is currently used mainly in the context of clinical research, divides breast cancers into four major types:

 

  • Luminal A: majority are lower-grade ER-positive cancers that are HER2 negative
  • Luminal B: majority are higher-grade ER-positive cancers that may be HER2 positive
  • HER2-enriched: The majority overexpress HER2 and do not express ER
  • Basal-like: majority by gene expression profiling resemble basally located myoepithelial cells and are ER-negative, HER2-negative

questions.stem: A baby is diagnosed with B cell leukemia. All of the following are good prognostic factors except? A. Hyperdiploidy B. Age < 1 year C. t(9;22) D. t(4;11)

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man presents to the emergency department with a 5-day history of fever, productive cough with yellow sputum, pleuritic chest pain, and shortness of breath. On physical examination, he has a temperature of 101.3°F, and auscultation of the lungs reveals crackles and decreased breath sounds in the right lower lobe. A chest X-ray shows a lobar consolidation in the right lower lobe. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause of his symptoms?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Streptococcal pneumonia

 

Clinical Summary:

 

  • 60-year-old man with:
    • Fever
    • Productive cough with yellow sputum
    • Pleuritic chest pain
    • Shortness of breath
    • Crackles + decreased breath sounds
  • Chest X-ray: Right lower lobe consolidation

 

All these are classical signs of lobar pneumonia, and the most common cause is:

 

Streptococcus pneumoniae (Pneumococcus)

 

  • Most common cause of community-acquired pneumonia in adults
  • Classically causes lobar consolidation
  • Often presents with:
    • Sudden onset
    • Fever, chills, pleuritic pain
    • Rust-colored or yellow sputum
  • Gram-positive lancet-shaped diplococci
  • Treatable with beta-lactams or macrolides

 

Other Options:

 

 

Summary:

 

  • Lobar consolidation + productive cough + elderly patient = typical pneumonia
  • Streptococcus pneumoniae is the most likely cause

questions.stem: A male patient suffers a trauma and is being brought to the emergency of a hospital. Since he needs an emergency lifesaving transfusion, which of the following can be safely transfused in him?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) O negative

 

O negative is the ideal blood to be transfused when there is no time available for blood grouping and cross matching. However, Rh+ cells may be transfused in older adults, postmenopausal women and life-threatening conditions.

questions.stem: A 75-year-old male presents with symptoms of fatigue, weight loss, and recurrent fevers. There is history of surgery for a malignancy couple of years back. Echocardiography demonstrates multiple small, sterile mobile masses attached along line of closure of the mitral and tricuspid valves. Which of the following underlying mechanisms is most likely responsible for the development of this cardiac manifestation?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Non bacterial thrombotic endocarditis

 

Case Summary:

 

Elderly male (75 years) with:

 

  • Fatigue, weight loss, recurrent fevers (suggestive of systemic illness)
  • Echocardiogram:
    • Multiple small, sterile masses
    • Located along the line of closure of mitral and tricuspid valves
  • Key feature: Sterile vegetations — points away from infection

 

Most Likely Diagnosis: NBTE (Non-bacterial thrombotic endocarditis)

 

Mechanism:

 

  • Sterile fibrin and platelet-rich thrombi form on normal or damaged valves
  • Common in:
    • Advanced malignancy (esp. mucinous adenocarcinomas)
    • Chronic debilitating diseases
    • Hypercoagulable states (e.g., antiphospholipid syndrome)
  • Vegetations are non-destructive, sterile, and often along line of valve closure

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Infective endocarditis: Involves infected vegetations, often with destruction of valve tissue and systemic infection — not “sterile”

 

Option B. Libman-Sacks endocarditis: Seen in SLE, vegetations on both sides of the valve leaflets or on chordae tendineae — not just along line of closure

 

Option D. Rheumatic endocarditis: Occurs post-streptococcal pharyngitis, involves Aschoff bodies and chronic scarring — not typical sterile vegetations seen here

questions.stem: With respect to thromboelastography, which of the following are true statements: 1. R time is dependent on the clotting factors 2. Platelet activity determines the maximum amplitude in the graph 3. LY30 represents the 30% lysis of the clot and depends on fibrinolytic activity 4. Alpha angle depends on the rate of fibrin deposition
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) 1, 2 and 4

 

Ly30 represents percentage amplitude reduction 30 minutes after maximum amplitude.

questions.stem: A girl presents with short stature, webbed neck, thick calves, shield -shaped chest, swelling of the ankle, and increased carrying angle. What is the likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml: Ans. A) Turner syndrome

questions.stem: A known patient of Burkitt lymphoma undergoes chemotherapy following which he develops tumor lysis syndrome. All of the following may be seen with tumor lysis syndrome except
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) Hypercalcemia

 

  • Tumor lysis syndrome is associated with Burkitt lymphoma, acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), chronic tumors (CLL) and uncommonly solid tumors.
  • It is associated with hypocalcemia and NOT hypercalcemia.
